what: A proposed chapter map for the second edition: the target nodes the ideas go to. Proposed by the librarian on 18 October 2026 from the survey's 18 topics, Dinis's three storyline articles (the opening, where do you land, connect the dots backwards) and the first storyline storyboard. It is the first answer to the editor's blocked issue 003 (the chapter map) and to task 1 of Start from the storyline; the editor owns the chapter map and Dinis decides it. Every chapter is 'proposed' until then. gravity: the centre of gravity the chapter leans to (explorer, villager, town-planner, all); character: the cast member it is written for first.

states.storyboarded: a storyboard exists for its part
states.reviewed: the reviewer and synthetic readers have had a round

chapters.title: You are lucky to be here
chapters.punchline: Wonder, not fear: you are starting out in the biggest change of your career, while the pieces are still landing.

chapters.title: Where do you land?
chapters.punchline: Maps before names, and the first thing to work out is your centre of gravity: explorer, villager or town planner.

chapters.title: Connect the dots backwards
chapters.punchline: Your path only makes sense looking back; learning is a lifelong skill you can finally shape to how you think; read this on paper.

chapters.title: Everyone who can brief an agent is a developer
chapters.punchline: The definition widened, and so did the door; here is what the briefing-only developer still cannot do.

chapters.title: Explorer coding, and the handover
chapters.punchline: Build to find out; then hand it to the people who will make it something others rely on; the prototype is the best brief.

chapters.title: Hired for the workflow
chapters.punchline: The one competitive advantage in 2026 is running agentic workflows; you are more technical than you think; it starts with the application.

chapters.title: Act as the job you want
chapters.punchline: If you are looking for a job you have time: do the job in public before you have it, make it linkable, put your CV online.

chapters.title: Publish, publish, publish: your own newsroom
chapters.punchline: A publishing loop you can copy on day one; small finished pieces; an article behind every answer.

chapters.title: Your first workspace
chapters.punchline: From a spreadsheet to a folder per person, in an afternoon; drafts never send; and why your agents should not run on your laptop.

chapters.title: How to work with agents
chapters.punchline: An agent is a session with a focus; the brief is the unit of work; one shared state across voice, chat and phone; and the trap of a rule per mistake.

chapters.title: Direction is the scarce skill
chapters.punchline: When anyone can build, choosing what to build, when to stop, and where a person belongs is what gets paid for; agents decide, people answer.

chapters.title: Facts, evidence and the record
chapters.punchline: Make fact-based decisions, as the cover says: count rather than remember, let the record check you, distrust self-reports.

chapters.title: Controlling your agent, and security for the agent era
chapters.punchline: Mandate, reach and the gap; hope versus enforcement; code is a liability; secrets never in the chat; learning to hack is still how you learn.

chapters.title: Open source
chapters.punchline: Nobody can lock you in; the fork next door; your first pull request.

chapters.title: Building blocks
chapters.punchline: Cloud as Lego, free models with your own key, git as a standard, serverless as ephemeral town planner services, what tokens cost.

chapters.title: Shipped means the user has it
chapters.punchline: Green does not mean live; tests that never run are not tests; go slow to go fast; five people who do not exist.

chapters.title: Graphs, memory and your future self
chapters.punchline: Think in graphs; maintain knowledge rather than perfect it; keep your work linkable and backed up for the person you will be.

chapters.title: Be a founder
chapters.punchline: The expert can build first now; the test is whether they miss it; pay after the value.

chapters.title: Civic responsibility
chapters.punchline: To hack means to solve problems; small countries can lead now that everyone can build; sovereignty is the ability to move.

chapters.title: How this book was made
chapters.punchline: The repository and the vault, the roles, the articles as briefs, the decisions, the graph, the loop; co-written with Claude, and the ratio shown.
